passes.candidate: Skip the unused live-purpose quota COUNT for a freshly present native-state update
passes.mechanism: Retain the caller-owned transaction, stable quota advisory lock, bounded expired cleanup and fresh existing-key lookup. Run the exact old quota COUNT only when that lookup is absent; preserve rotated-key deletion and protected upsert.
passes.reason: Accepted: one unused SQL roundtrip is removed from every freshly present update. At the real 10,000 active ACCESS-state quota all three native transaction pairs improve35.8–44.2%. One-row timings are noisy, so no universal small-update latency claim is made.

passes.candidate: Cap native rotation-read materialization at the two rows needed to detect duplicates
passes.mechanism: Prototype LIMIT2 on the same fresh bounded physical-key query: zero is absent, one is decrypted/validated and two or more still raise the same redacted duplicate error.

limitations: Measurements are synthetic native local PostgreSQL18 and installed SDK workloads, not production p95 or browser navigation claims.
The one-row quota update has mixed paired latency variation; the robust benefit is one unused query removed and the near-quota large-case gain.
Callback policy CPU/parse-count gain is consistent; full database-backed provider authorization is dominated by SQL variability and has no stable final latency gain.
Subclass policy retains its public extensibility and original loop; the final negative control has small mixed timing variation.
All owned measurement schemas are dropped by fixture teardown; no real credentials, production authority cache, PG lifecycle operation or dependency/config change is introduced.
Root owns full unchanged make check, normal hooks, hosted CI, admin merge/deploy, original workspace sync and authenticated live verification after both scopes seal.
These five measured candidates do not prove that no future optimization is possible.
